questions.text: What is the primary benefit of spreading investments across different companies, sectors, and asset types?
options: It reduces the impact of a downturn in any single area
It requires predicting which company will perform best
questions.explanation: Spreading investments lowers the chance that a single area's decline will heavily affect the whole portfolio.

questions.text: What happens to a portfolio's risk level when some holdings grow significantly while others remain unchanged over time?
options: The portfolio's asset allocation shifts, potentially increasing risk
The risk level stays exactly the same
The portfolio becomes more conservative than originally intended
The investor must immediately sell all holdings
questions.explanation: As some investments grow, their share of the portfolio rises, changing the original risk balance.

questions.text: True or false: Diversification means you do not need to predict which company will perform best; you rely on the overall growth of the economy rather than the luck of a single business.
questions.explanation: Diversification removes the need to pick a single winning company.

questions.text: True or false: Past performance is a guarantee of future returns.
questions.explanation: Past performance never guarantees future results.
